props.title: Catch-22

sections.content: Mike Nichols' adaptation of Joseph Heller's satirical masterpiece Catch-22 (1970) stands as one of Hollywood's most ambitious attempts to capture the absurdity of war bureaucracy. Following Alan Arkin's perfectly-cast Yossarian, the film's dark comedy approach influenced later war satires like MASH (1970) and Three Kings (1999). The film's non-linear structure and surreal tone set it apart from straightforward war films of its era like Patton (1970), instead creating a deliberately disorienting experience that mirrors its protagonist's psychological state.

sections.content: The film arrived at a crucial moment in American cinema, during the Vietnam War era when anti-war sentiment was peaking. Like Dr. Strangelove (1964), it uses absurdist humor to expose military madness, though Nichols opts for a more naturalistic approach than Kubrick's broad satire. The film's influence extends to modern war comedies like In the Loop (2009) and War Machine (2017), which similarly tackle military bureaucracy's inherent contradictions.

Cinematographer David Watkin's sun-bleached Mediterranean visuals create a deceptively beautiful backdrop for the horror and madness, a technique later echoed in Apocalypse Now (1979) and Full Metal Jacket (1987). The all-star cast including Orson Welles, Jon Voight, and Bob Newhart delivers performances that walk the razor's edge between comedy and tragedy, establishing a template for later war satires. movies.title: War Machine
movies.slug: Brad Pitt stars as a general trying to win an unwinnable war in this satire of modern military leadership.

sections.content: While Catch-22 struggled at the box office (partially due to competition from MASH), its influence on war satire remains profound. Films like Buffalo Soldiers (2001) and Four Lions (2010) continue its tradition of using dark humor to expose institutional absurdity. The film's central paradox - that one must be crazy to want to fly dangerous missions, but requesting to be relieved of duty demonstrates sanity - has become a cultural touchstone for describing impossible situations.
